---
title: "Does it meet the 50 g mass budget with ballast fitted?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

```{python}
ENTRY_CEILING = 90.0   # s for this render, granted by the user
SOLVE_BUDGET = 15.0     # s for any one solve
PROBE_POOL = 200.0        # s granted for the probe
PROBE_SPENT = 13.0      # s the probe actually used

plane = get_airplane()
mass, cg = get_mass_properties(plane, area_density=0.1744, foam_thickness=0.005)

# From 2026-09-24-01-how-much-nose-ballast-is-needed-with-wings-at-the-rear
nose_ballast_mass = 0.0
total_mass = mass + nose_ballast_mass
```

**Answer.** Yes. The airframe mass is [`{python} f"{mass*1000:.1f}"`]{.key} g. As found in [How much nose ballast is needed with wings at the rear?](2026-09-24-01-how-much-nose-ballast-is-needed-with-wings-at-the-rear.qmd), it requires no nose ballast because the center of gravity is already forward of the required position. This leaves the total mass at [`{python} f"{total_mass*1000:.1f}"`]{.key} g, well under the 50 g budget.

::: {.callout-tip}
## New user specifications
Asked of the user, 2026-09-29:

1. **mass budget: 50 g** — Target for total mass.
:::

```{python}
#| label: fig-mass
#| fig-cap: "Total aircraft mass compared to the 50 g mass budget."
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 4))
ax.bar(["Airframe", "Total Mass", "Budget"], 
       [mass * 1000, total_mass * 1000, 50],
       color=["#1f77b4", "#2ca02c", "#7f7f7f"])
ax.axhline(50, color="gray", linestyle="--", zorder=0)
ax.set_ylabel("Mass (g)")
plt.show()
```
